summary: Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit analysis (reported 7 June 2026) projects Wales will deliver only 14 percent of its 2030 woodland creation target, within a UK-wide cumulative shortfall of about 41,000 hectares by 2030. Over 70 percent of the carbon removal needed to 2050 depends on trees planted in the next five years, and polling shows 66 percent of Welsh adults support significantly increased planting. Official provisional statistics published by Forest Research on 25 June 2026 bear the projection out: only 680 hectares of new woodland were created in Wales in the year to 31 March 2026, about 10 percent of the 6,000 hectare annual target and down from 960 hectares in 2024-25.
title: ECIU analysis: Wales projected to deliver just 14 percent of its 2030 tree planting target
